$comment: Primary-source oracle — ACA / Medicare cases: the 2026 §36B applicable-percentage schedule with the reinstated 400% cliff (including whole-percent mid-band interpolation at 177.5% with production's raw-percentage smoothing pinned as a divergence record, the documented (400%,401%) cliff-sliver production bug, and the §86-vs-§36B dual-MAGI case), the disclosed rough-benchmark fallback, and month-aware IRMAA proration. Expected values derived independently from the cited sources; never from production code.

rp-2025-25.name: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-25 — Applicable Percentage Table for 2026
rp-2025-25.publication: Rev. Proc. 2025-25 (published 2025; verified from the IRS PDF)

hhs-fpl-2025.name: HHS 2025 poverty guidelines (prior-year FPL lag per Rev. Proc. 2014-37 §4.02)

irs-ptc-qa.name: IRS — Questions and answers on the Premium Tax Credit
irs-ptc-qa.identifier: PTC = benchmark SLCSP premium minus the expected contribution (MAGI x applicable percentage); household income measured against the FPL

cms-2026.name: CMS — 2026 Medicare Parts A & B Premiums and Deductibles
cms-2026.identifier: 2026 Part B standard premium $202.90/mo; joint-return IRMAA tier 1 (> $218,000 to $274,000): Part B $81.20/mo, Part D $14.50/mo

poms-hi-01101-031.name: SSA POMS HI 01101.031 — How IRMAA is calculated
poms-hi-01101-031.identifier: IRMAA applies per enrolled beneficiary; Part B and Part D adjustments are separate amounts (35/50/65/80/85% cost shares); premium year 2026 tables match the CMS fact sheet

i8962-2020.name: IRS Instructions for Form 8962 (2020) — the last pre-ARPA edition (Worksheet 2 + applicable-figure Table 2 mechanics)
i8962-2020.publication: 2020 tax-year edition (pre-ARPA rules the 2026 cliff reinstates)
i8962-2020.identifier: Worksheet 2 line 5 compares household income DIRECTLY with 4.0 x the FPL — 'more than' -> not eligible for the PTC, BEFORE any rounding; only an eligible household's income-as-percentage-of-FPL is then rounded DOWN to a whole percent (Form 8962 line 5) for the Table 2 applicable-figure lookup

usc-36b.name: 26 U.S.C. §36B(d)(2)(B) — ACA household-income MAGI definition
usc-36b.identifier: ACA MAGI = AGI increased by (i) foreign earned income, (ii) tax-exempt interest, and (iii) the portion of Social Security benefits NOT included in gross income under §86 — the full benefit counts, unlike the federal/IRMAA MAGI which carries only the §86-taxable portion

usc-86.name: 26 U.S.C. §86 — taxation of Social Security benefits (base amounts + tier composition)
usc-86.publication: statutory (OLRC current edition; base amounts fixed since 1993)
usc-86.identifier: Single base $25,000 / adjusted base $34,000; 50%/85% tiers feed the taxable portion the §36B(d)(2)(B) add-back is computed against

cases.description: 2026 PTC, Single household of 1 at exactly 200% FPL: the 6.60% applicable percentage (200-250 band floor) applies.
derivation: MAGI = 2.0 * 15,650 = 31,300 -> 200% FPL exactly; the 150-200 band is upper-exclusive, so the 200-250 band's floor figure 6.60% applies.
Expected contribution = round(3,130,000 cents * 0.066) = 206,580 cents.

cases.description: 2026 PTC at exactly 400% FPL: still eligible (the cliff is strictly ABOVE 400%), flat 9.96%.
derivation: MAGI = 4.0 * 15,650 = 62,600 -> exactly 400%; the 300-400 band is inclusive at 400 -> 9.96%.

cases.description: 2026 PTC mid-band at 177.5% FPL: MATERIALLY between two whole percents, so Form 8962 line 5's round-DOWN-to-a-whole-percent step is genuinely discriminated from raw-percentage interpolation — floor(177.5) = 177 -> 5.49%, while interpolating the raw 177.5% would give 5.52%. `expected` records the correct truncate-then-interpolate answer; `expectedCurrentEngine` records production aca-ptc.ts's raw-percentage interpolation (its deliberate smoothing — see the whole-percent comment in computeAcaPtc) so the $8.34 divergence stays visible. If production adopts the whole-percent Table 2 lookup, the engine pin fails loudly and this flips to a normal agreement case.
cases.tolerance: within $1 (whole-percent figure exact; engine-divergence record exact)
derivation: MAGI = 1.775 * 15,650 = 27,778.75 -> raw 177.5% FPL (materially between whole percents); Form 8962 line 5 rounds DOWN to 177%.
CORRECT Table 2 figure at 177%: 4.19% + ((177-150)/50) * (6.60%-4.19%) = 4.19% + 0.54*2.41% = 5.4914% -> published-table rounding to 4 decimals -> 5.49%.
Expected contribution = round(2,777,875 cents * 0.0549) = 152,505 cents; benchmark $600/mo = 720,000 -> PTC = 720,000 - 152,505 = 567,495 cents ($5,674.95).

CURRENT ENGINE (raw-percentage interpolation, truncation skipped): 4.19% + ((177.5-150)/50) * 2.41% = 5.5155% -> 4-decimal rounding -> 5.52%; contribution = round(2,777,875 * 0.0552) = 153,339 -> PTC = 720,000 - 153,339 = 566,661 cents ($5,666.61) — $8.34 less subsidy than the Worksheet answer.

cases.description: 2026 PTC just above 401% FPL: the pre-ARPA cliff returns — $0 PTC (Rev. Proc. 2025-25's table ends at 400%).
derivation: MAGI $62,757 > 4.0 * 15,650 = $62,600 -> ineligible per Form 8962 Worksheet 2 (household income compared directly with 4 x FPL, before any rounding).

PTC = 0; tier above-400-cliff. (At 401.0% FPL the production engine's floored-percent comparison agrees with Worksheet 2; the (400%, 401%) sliver where they diverge is the separate known-bug case below.)

cases.description: KNOWN BUG: 2026 household at 400.5% FPL. Form 8962 Worksheet 2 makes it INELIGIBLE (income $62,678.25 > 4 x FPL = $62,600, compared before any truncation), but production aca-ptc.ts floors the FPL percent to 400 BEFORE the cliff comparison and wrongly keeps the household subsidized. expectedCorrect records the Worksheet 2 answer; expectedCurrentEngine records today's (incorrect) production output so the divergence stays visible until the production fix lands.
derivation: CORRECT (i8962-2020 Worksheet 2): 62,678.25 > 62,600 -> not eligible for the PTC; $0.

CURRENT ENGINE (the bug): floor(400.5) = 400 is not > 400 -> treated as eligible; the raw 400.5% misses every band so the engine clamps to the top band's 9.96% -> expected contribution = round(6,267,825 * 0.0996) = 624,275 -> PTC = 720,000 - 624,275 = 95,725 cents.

cases.description: One Social-Security-receiving household, BOTH statutory MAGIs at once: the federal/IRMAA MAGI carries only the §86-TAXABLE benefit portion, while the §36B(d)(2)(B) ACA MAGI adds back the FULL benefit (including the nontaxable portion). ACA-covered (non-Medicare) member near the 400% cliff: the add-back moves the household from the 200-250 band (federal MAGI, 249.2% FPL) to 396.2% FPL.
cases.tolerance: SS/MAGI cents within $1; PTC within $1 (band + tier selection exact)
derivation: Retiree born 1963-04-15 (age 63 in 2026): claimed Social Security early, on ACA Marketplace coverage until Medicare at 65. Gross SS 36,000; pre-tax IRA withdrawal 26,000; no other income.
Federal/IRMAA MAGI = 26,000 + 13,000 (taxable SS only) = 39,000 -> 3,900,000 cents (249.2% FPL — would sit mid-band if it were, wrongly, fed to §36B).

§36B(d)(2)(B) ACA MAGI = 39,000 + (36,000 - 13,000) nontaxable add-back = 62,000 -> 6,200,000 cents -> 62,000/15,650 = 396.17% FPL (whole-percent 396) -> flat 9.96% band, still eligible (below the 400% cliff).

Conflation guard: computing the PTC from the FEDERAL MAGI instead would use the 200-250 band's figure at 249% (8.40%) -> 840,000 - round(3,900,000*0.084) = 512,400 cents — $2,899.20 too generous, so a dropped add-back cannot pass.

cases.description: Disclosed rough ACA benchmark fallback: per-member age-priced monthly premium summed over each member's covered months — an approximation, NOT an exchange SLCSP quote.
cases.tolerance: within $50/year vs the independent workbook; assumptions and direction asserted separately
derivation: Disclosed assumptions (product calibration, not statute): $700/mo at age 60, +5% per year of age, per covered member per covered month.
Member B age 60, 4 months: 70,000 cents * 4 = 280,000.
Household total = 1,206,100 cents ($12,061.00). Direction: premium must rise with age (age-62 monthly > age-60 monthly).

cases.description: Month-aware IRMAA, 2026 MFJ lookback MAGI $250,000 (joint tier 1): Part B prorated over 6 enrolled months, Part D over 12 — the two parts prorate independently.
cases.tolerance: exact (coverage-month counts and table lookup exact; CMS dollars exact)
derivation: Beneficiary 1: B 6/12 months -> round(97,440*6/12) = 48,720; D 12/12 -> 17,400. Beneficiary 2: not enrolled -> 0.
Household total = 66,120 cents ($661.20).
